newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP AFTERNOON UPDATE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP AFTERNOON UPDATE.

text.p: THREE TO BE CHARGED OVER BLACKHAWK DISASTER
Three Army Officers are to face disciplinary charges in the wake of last year's Blackhawk helicopter disaster in north Queensland.
The charges relate to negligent performance of duty.
Eighteen servicemen were killed when two helicopters collided during night exercises in what was the Army's worst peacetime disaster.

The three officers will be charged under the Defence Force Discipline Act, with the charges to be heard by a Commanding Officer, who will then decide whether they should be dismissed or referred to further hearings.
The move follows an extensive inquiry into the tragedy that found the collision was the result of the inexperience of the aircrew involved and the unserviceability of the aircraft.
TOURISM INDUSTRY MAY BACK GST
A goods and services tax could get support from the Tourism industry.
Hotel, Motel, and Accomodation Association of Australia Chief Executive, John McKernan, said if the Industry was treated as an export earner it would be exempt from certain aspects of a GST.
He said that would be fairer than the present tax system which includes a bed tax in New South Wales, and the Liquor excise problems.
Mr McKernan said a tourism tax summit has been organised for next month.
"The Hospitality-Tourism industry doesn't want to be caught with its pants down, so to speak.," Mr McKernan said.

"We want to be able to go to any inquiry, any presentation that's required, and talk sensibly about what the industry wants. And of course in a goods and services tax, we expect trade-offs. Therefore it's just not an increase on top of what's already there," he said.
WARNING TAX REFORM COULD HIT ELDERLY
The Council on the Ageing has warned tax reform for older people could mean they are much worse off.
The Council said most older people were on fixed incomes, which did not attract tax, so an indirect tax on basic living costs would mean a massive impost.

Executive director Denys Correll said it was possible for the Government to offer compensation, but there were problems in ensuring they were not worse off and the value of the compensation was maintained over time.
Mr Correll said there was also a problem with compensation for those living on income from shares, investments, annuities and superannuation.
He said older people had already paid tax on money they had invested, and under a GST they will be effectively taxed twice.
PERKINS SAYS KOWALSKI STILL MAIN RIVAL
In swimming...despite last night's win in the 1500 metres at the Pan Pac meet in Japan by Grant Hackett, world record holder Kieran Perkins believes Daniel Kowalski is still his main rival.
Perkins says at a meet such as the Pan Pacs, times are a more accurate guide than gold medals, and the 17-year-old is yet to post a competitive 1500 metre time.
Perkins says it's likely to be the proven performers who will pose the greatest challenge.
"You've got to go with the proven competitors and that's Daniel," he said.
"Daniel's done the times. He's been there. Grant Hackett hasn't broken 15 minutes for the 1500 yet. It's as simple as that."
REIFFEL BACKS WARNE'S AFTER-MATCH CELEBRATION
Australian cricketer, Paul Reiffel, has backed his team-mate, Shane Warne, after Warne was criticised for his enthusiastic celebrating, after the team's Ashes win.
Reiffel returned home today, to be with his wife, who is expecting their first child, and is having a difficult pregnancy.
He says Warne put so much of himself into the team's effort, his enjoyment was understandable.
"He did it for us really," Reiffel said.

"He didn't get the wickets, but he was the energy out there and when he got off the ground it's hard for him just to stop. So obviously the crowd got him going and he's allowed to enjoy success. I think he does so much for the team and I think his energy was fantastic."
And despite initially missing out on selection for the tour, Reiffel says he's not worrying about whether he proved a point to the selectors.
"I never really thought I had a point to prove. So I didn't go over there with that in mind, so that's for someone else to say, not for me."
CHARGES COST FOOTBALLER SPONSORSHIP
The manager of Sydney Swans footballer, Tony Lockett says the full-forward lost some sponsorship deals, because of theft and fraud charges against him.
All of the 46 charges relating to greyhound breeding matters, have now been offically withdrawn.
It was alleged Lockett's champion greyhound, Malawai's Prince did not deliver stud services as promised.
37 of the charges were dropped two weeks ago and the remaining nine were dropped today.
Prosectutor, Mirko Bagaric, told the Dandenong Magistrates Court there was no reasonable prospect for conviction.
Lockett's manager, Robert Hessions, says the footballer is relieved the charges have been withdrawn and wants to re-establish his reputation in the sporting community.
"People these days want all the profile people to be squeeky clean, and there was this slur that's been hanging around," Mr Hessions said.
"And fortunately now it's all been cleared up. And hopefully those sponsors will come back, and we'll look at any sponsors who want to have a talk to us now," he said.
